reading: A beginning that has already happened and has not found its shape. The seed is in the ground with the whole weight of the ground on top of it. Something has started in you. It is real, and it is tangled, pushing up through more than you thought would be in the way. The root goes down a long way before any green shows.

Then there is the face people brace against. The storm builds, the first thunder comes up out of the ground, and the rain just does not fall. It can feel like the floor went out from under you, like the thing to do is grab whatever is closest and hold on. But the old word under chaos never meant a mess. It meant the open ground, the space a thing gets born into. The coming-apart is the room the new thing needs.

What it asks of you is small and slow, the work of someone at a loom. Not forcing the rain. Not standing frozen in all that charge either. You sort one thread, then the next. You find the two or three people who will hold the corners with you. The whole of it is already here, pooled like oil in the press, spreading inside you and not bright yet. Stay small. Let the beginning be difficult.
